title: Scale of the Solar System
seo_title: Grade 8 Scale of the Solar System Worksheets: Planet Sizes, Distances and Scale Models
standard_text: Analyze and interpret data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on the scale of the solar system (NGSS MS-ESS1-3): comparing planet and Sun diameters, distances in AU, scale models and light travel time. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Divide to compare sizes; use AU for distances.
key_sub: The Sun is about 109 Earths wide, and the planets are spread out over huge distances. Most of the solar system is empty space.
body_html:
How to think about it

Objects in the solar system have enormous differences in size and distance. Use data and ratios to compare them.

  • Divide to compare sizes: Sun 1,392,000 km ÷ Earth 12,800 km ≈ 109; Jupiter is about 11 times wider than Earth.
  • Distances are measured in astronomical units (1 AU = Earth-Sun distance ≈ 150 million km). Neptune is about 30 AU away.
  • In a scale model, every size or distance is multiplied by the same factor. Real distances are so large compared with sizes that most of the solar system is empty space.
Example

Saturn 120,500 km, Earth 12,800 km. How many times wider?

120,500 ÷ 12,800 ≈ 9.4

Answer: about 9 times

Example

1 AU = 10 cm. Jupiter at 5.2 AU?

5.2 × 10

Answer: about 52 cm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the planets are evenly spaced.
  • Subtracting when you should divide to compare sizes.
  • Using one scale for sizes and another for distances without saying so.

faq.q: How big is the Sun compared with Earth?
faq.a: The Sun's diameter is about 109 times Earth's diameter.
The average distance between Earth and the Sun, about 150 million kilometers.

faq.q: Why is it hard to make a scale model of the solar system?
faq.a: If the planets are big enough to see, the distances between them become huge, often hundreds of meters or more.

items.q: Are the planets evenly spaced from the Sun?
c: No. The outer planets are much farther apart than the inner planets.
